questions.question_text: There are four numbers such that average of first two numbers is 1 more than the first number, average of first three numbers is 2 more than average of first two numbers, and average of first four numbers is 3 more than average of first three numbers. Then, the difference between the largest and the smallest numbers, is
questions.explanation_text:
We need to find what "Average of first two numbers is 1 more than the first number" means:

p+q2=p+1\tfrac{p+q}{2} = p + 12p+q​=p+1

p+q=2p+2p + q = 2p + 2p+q=2p+2

q=p+2q = p + 2q=p+2

The second number is always 2 more than the first number.

For "Average of first three numbers is 2 more than average of first two numbers":

We know the average of first two numbers is p+1p + 1p+1 from the previous condition.

So: p+q+r3=(p+1)+2=p+3\tfrac{p+q+r}{3} = (p + 1) + 2 = p + 33p+q+r​=(p+1)+2=p+3

p+q+r=3p+9p + q + r = 3p + 9p+q+r=3p+9

Since we know q=p+2q = p + 2q=p+2, substituting:

p+(p+2)+r=3p+9p + (p + 2) + r = 3p + 9p+(p+2)+r=3p+9

2p+2+r=3p+92p + 2 + r = 3p + 92p+2+r=3p+9

r=3p+9−2p−2=p+7r = 3p + 9 - 2p - 2 = p + 7r=3p+9−2p−2=p+7

The third number is 7 more than the first number.

For "Average of first four numbers is 3 more than average of first three numbers":

We know the average of first three numbers is p+3p + 3p+3 from the previous condition.

So: p+q+r+s4=(p+3)+3=p+6\tfrac{p+q+r+s}{4} = (p + 3) + 3 = p + 64p+q+r+s​=(p+3)+3=p+6

p+q+r+s=4p+24p + q + r + s = 4p + 24p+q+r+s=4p+24

Substituting our known values q=p+2q = p + 2q=p+2 and r=p+7r = p + 7r=p+7:

p+(p+2)+(p+7)+s=4p+24p + (p + 2) + (p + 7) + s = 4p + 24p+(p+2)+(p+7)+s=4p+24

3p+9+s=4p+243p + 9 + s = 4p + 243p+9+s=4p+24

s=4p+24−3p−9=p+15s = 4p + 24 - 3p - 9 = p + 15s=4p+24−3p−9=p+15

The fourth number is 15 more than the first number.

Our four numbers are: ppp, p+2p + 2p+2, p+7p + 7p+7, p+15p + 15p+15

Notice that regardless of what ppp is, the pattern remains the same:

Smallest number: ppp

Largest number: p+15p + 15p+15

Difference between largest and smallest = (p+15)−p=15(p + 15) - p = 15(p+15)−p=15

The differences between consecutive numbers are 2, 5, and 8, creating a specific pattern that always results in a total spread of 15.

Therefore, the difference between the largest and smallest numbers is 15.

We need to find the sum of all four-digit numbers formed using four distinct non-zero digits a, b, c, and d, where each digit appears exactly once in every number.

We have 4 choices for the first position, 3 remaining choices for the second position, 2 for the third, and 1 for the last position. So: 4×3×2×1=244 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 244×3×2×1=24.

Since we're forming ALL possible arrangements, each digit will appear an equal number of times in each position.

Each digit appears in each position exactly 24÷4=624 \div 4 = 624÷4=6 times.

Out of 24 numbers, digit 'a' will be in the thousands place 6 times, hundreds place 6 times, tens place 6 times, and units place 6 times. Same for b, c, and d.

For any digit x, its total contribution across all 24 numbers is:

6 times in thousands place: 6×x×1000=6000x6 \times x \times 1000 = 6000x6×x×1000=6000x

6 times in hundreds place: 6×x×100=600x6 \times x \times 100 = 600x6×x×100=600x

6 times in tens place: 6×x×10=60x6 \times x \times 10 = 60x6×x×10=60x

6 times in units place: 6×x×1=6x6 \times x \times 1 = 6x6×x×1=6x

Total contribution of digit x = 6000x+600x+60x+6x=6666x6000x + 600x + 60x + 6x = 6666x6000x+600x+60x+6x=6666x

To find (a+b+c+d)(a + b + c + d)(a+b+c+d), we divide: 153310÷6666153310 \div 6666153310÷6666

153310÷6666=23.001...153310 \div 6666 = 23.001...153310÷6666=23.001...

Since (a+b+c+d)(a + b + c + d)(a+b+c+d) must be a whole number (sum of digits), we take the integer part: a+b+c+d=23a + b + c + d = 23a+b+c+d=23

If a+b+c+d=23a + b + c + d = 23a+b+c+d=23, then:

6666×23=1533186666 \times 23 = 1533186666×23=153318

Comparing with our equation:

153318=153310+n153318 = 153310 + n153318=153310+n

n=8n = 8n=8

n=8n = 8n=8 is indeed a single-digit natural number as required, and our calculation checks out perfectly.
